{"parentUuid":"ccda9d56-089f-468a-b6d0-80c4bd81edc7","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-fable-5-1","id":"msg_011CfYC9WAgrDJzeQaNKZMiV","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01M2yqPEYTNqfg4mGWFzsB1k","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/jonc/code/theailab-net-dev/dev-notes/macbook_stt_20260929.md","content":"# MacBook STT (speech-to-text) fix: Orca Cmd+E, macOS Dictation, DJI mic\n\nDate: 2026-09-29 · Orchestrator: Claude Code (claude-fable-5-1), session run from an Orca pane\nRelated: [stt_claude-code-macos_20260921.md](stt_claude-code-macos_20260921.md),\n[ade-orca-workflow_20260923.md](ade-orca-workflow_20260923.md),\n[macbook-config_20260905.md](macbook-config_20260905.md)\n\n## TL;DR\n\n| Symptom | Root cause | Fix |\n|---|---|---|\n| Cmd+E did nothing in Orca on the MacBook (repeat presses typed `eeee`) | MacBook Orca had voice enabled but **no STT model selected** (`settings.voice.sttModel = \"\"`), so Orca never claimed Cmd+E and the key fell through to the terminal pane | Orca → Settings → Voice → select and download **Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 (int8)**. Cmd+E now works |\n| Cmd+E did nothing in standalone Ghostty | Expected: Orca's dictation is scoped to Orca windows, and Ghostty has no STT and no Cmd+E binding | Use a system-wide STT (macOS Dictation or Whispering) for non-Orca apps |\n| macOS Dictation showed the blue mic in TextEdit but produced no text | Mic source \"Automatic\" picked **Wireless Mic Rx** (DJI receiver) while the DJI transmitter was asleep or off, so it was sending silence | Woke the transmitter; Dictation now transcribes |\n| DJI transmitter keeps going to sleep | DJI **Transmitter Auto Off** (about 15 min with no link) plus non-disableable power-saving sleep | Receiver → swipe down → Transmitter Settings → Transmitter Auto Off = OFF (Mic Mini: DJI Mimo app) |\n\nFinal state: **Orca Cmd+E dictation works (Parakeet v3); macOS Dictation works (Globe twice); DJI mic works when awake.**\n\n## 1. Environment (the key discovery)\n\nThe problem report said \"this MacBook\", but the Claude session was running on a **different machine**.\nOrca runs as a host runtime on the Mac Studio with the MacBook attached as a remote client, so\nOrca terminal panes on the MacBook execute their shells on the Mac Studio.\n\n| | Mac Studio (runtime host) | MacBook Pro (where you type) |\n|---|---|---|\n| Hostname / model | `Mac-Studio` / `Mac16,9` | `Jons-MacBook-Pro-7.local` / `Mac16,1` |\n| Tailscale IP | 100.126.217.74 | 100.82.72.91 (`jons-macbook-pro`) |\n| Orca version | 1.4.210 | 1.4.215 |\n| Orca voice `sttModel` (before fix) | `parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-int8` (downloaded 2026-09-23) | `\"\"` (none) |\n| Physical keyboard | none connected (Magic Keyboard \"Not Connected\") | built-in, plus an external PC-layout keyboard (vendor 9610 / product 73) |\n| Secure Input | held by `loginwindow` (PID 1340): screen locked, normal for a headless host | none |\n\nHow the topology was established:\n- `echo $TERM_PROGRAM` → `Orca`; the parent chain of the session is an `Orca Helper` on the Studio.\n- `~/Library/Application Support/orca/orca-devices.json` on the Studio lists a paired **\"Runtime 9/24/2026\"** device, `lastSeenAt` within about 45 s of \"now\".\n- `lsof -nP -iTCP:6768 -sTCP:ESTABLISHED` → Orca (pid 740) has websocket connections from **100.82.72.91**.\n- `tailscale status` → 100.82.72.91 = `jons-macbook-pro`.\n\n**Lesson:** anything typed into an Orca pane runs on the **Studio**. The first MacBook diagnostic run\ncame back with Studio data (same `loginwindow` PID 1340, same voice settings). Diagnostics for\nthe MacBook must run in **Terminal.app on the MacBook** (check `hostname` first).\n\n## 2. How Orca dictation works (from the 1.4.210 app bundle)\n\nExtracted `/Applications/Orca.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar` (via `npx @electron/asar extract`) and traced the key path:\n\n1. **Keybinding table** (`keybindings-*.js`): `{id: \"voice.dictation\", title: \"Dictation\", scope: \"global\", defaultBindings: [\"Mod+E\"]}`. `Mod+E` is the *only* default use of Cmd+E in Orca.\n2. **Main process** (`main/index.js`), `webContents.on(\"before-input-event\")`: the key maps to `{type: \"dictationKeyDown\"}`, then:\n   ```js\n   let t = settings.voice;\n   return !t?.enabled || !t.sttModel || (t.dictationMode ?? \"toggle\") === \"hold\"\n     ? false                                         // NOT handled → key falls through to the pane\n     : (e.preventDefault(), webContents.send(\"ui:dictationKeyDown\"), true)\n   ```\n3. **Renderer** (`DictationController-*.js`): `onDictationKeyDown` starts or stops recording only if `voice.enabled && voice.sttModel`.\n4. **Engine**: `Resources/node_modules/sherpa-onnx-darwin-arm64/` (sherpa-onnx + onnxruntime 1.23.2) runs in `stt-worker.js`. Models are downloaded from Hugging Face (`csukuangfj/sherpa-onnx-nemo-parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-int8`) into `~/Library/Application Support/orca/speech-models/<model>/` (`encoder.int8.onnx` is about 652 MB, plus decoder, joiner and `tokens.txt`).\n\nSo with `sttModel: \"\"`, Orca deliberately returns `false`, Cmd+E is passed to the terminal, and nothing starts. This explains the MacBook symptom exactly.\n\nRelevant settings, in `~/Library/Application Support/orca/profiles/local-default/orca-data.json` → `settings.voice`:\n```json\n{\"enabled\": true, \"sttModel\": \"parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-int8\", \"modelsDir\": \"\", \"language\": \"en\",\n \"dictationMode\": \"toggle\", \"terminalConfirmBeforeInsert\": false, \"microphoneDeviceId\": null}\n```\nCustom keybindings would live in `~/.orca/keybindings.json` (absent on both machines, so defaults apply).\n`settings.terminalShortcutPolicy = \"orca-first\"`.\n\n## 3. Debugging timeline\n\n1. **Explored the Studio (wrong machine, useful baseline).** Found Orca (Electron 43.7, v1.4.210), Ghostty, and Whispering (installed, not running).\n   All Studio-side checks passed:\n   - The keybinding is the default `Mod+E`, with no user override.\n   - The only plugin, `stablyai.orca-navigation-shortcuts`, binds `Mod+Alt+T/F/G`, so it doesn't conflict.\n   - No hotkey or remap apps are running (Karabiner, Raycast, BTT, Hammerspoon, skhd, …); `hidutil` UserKeyMapping is `(null)`; there are no `NSUserKeyEquivalents`.\n   - Mic TCC: `com.stablyai.orca` allowed (2026-09-23), and the app has the `com.apple.security.device.audio-input` entitlement.\n   - Speech engine and model files are present.\n2. **Tried to send Cmd+E via `osascript`/System Events.** It hung on an Automation permission prompt, so I killed it.\n   If a \"Orca wants to control System Events\" dialog appeared, answer *Don't Allow*.\n3. **User symptom report:** Cmd+E, with or without Shift, does nothing on the first press and types `e` on repeat presses, in both Orca and Ghostty.\n   That pointed below the app layer. The Orca lock file named the host `Mac-Studio.local`, which led to the topology discovery in §1.\n4. **SSH to the MacBook** (`ssh -o BatchMode=yes jonc@100.82.72.91`): Remote Login is on but password-only, so no key access.\n   Stopped rather than work around it. Side effect: the MacBook's ED25519 host key was added to the Studio's `~/.ssh/known_hosts`.\n5. **First \"MacBook\" diagnostics were really Studio output** (run from an Orca pane): the same `loginwindow` Secure Input PID 1340, identical voice settings. Re-ran in Terminal.app.\n6. **Real MacBook diagnostics:**\n   - The TextEdit test (Cmd+C/V, Cmd+T) worked normally, so the Command key is fine.\n   - No Secure Input and no hotkey apps; UniversalControl only.\n   - `hidutil` is `(null)`.\n   - `modifiermapping.0-0-0` (built-in keyboard) is identity.\n   - `modifiermapping.9610-73-0` (external PC keyboard) swaps Cmd↔Option on both sides. That's the usual setup for a PC-layout keyboard and not the cause (usage `0xE2`=L-Opt, `0xE3`=L-Cmd, `0xE6`=R-Opt, `0xE7`=R-Cmd).\n   - **Orca voice `sttModel: ''`**: this was the root cause.\n7. **Fix applied by the user:** selected and downloaded Parakeet v3 in MacBook Orca → **Cmd+E works**.\n8. **macOS Dictation (for non-Orca apps).** Enabled with a Cmd+D shortcut. The blue mic showed in TextEdit but produced no text.\n   - Clarified that Dictation streams text live; there is no separate stop-and-transcribe step. Stop it with the shortcut, Esc, or by clicking the mic.\n   - Changed the shortcut to **Press Globe twice**, because Cmd+D is Ghostty's default \"split right\" and a system-wide shortcut would take it away from every app.\n   - Mic source \"Automatic\" had picked **Wireless Mic Rx** (the DJI receiver). The transmitter was asleep, so it was sending silence. Turning the transmitter on fixed it.\n9. **DJI transmitter sleep:** see §5.\n\n## 4. Final configuration\n\n**MacBook, Orca (Settings → Voice)**\n- Voice: enabled · Model: `parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-int8` (local, offline) · Mode: toggle · Language: en\n- Shortcut: **Cmd+E** (default `voice.dictation`); press once to start and again to stop. Works only while an Orca window has focus.\n\n**MacBook, macOS Dictation (System Settings → Keyboard → Dictation)**\n- On · Shortcut: **Press Globe (🌐) twice** · Language: English (US), on-device model downloaded\n- Microphone source: Automatic, which currently resolves to **Wireless Mic Rx** (DJI). If Dictation shows the mic but types nothing, check the transmitter first, or pin the source to *MacBook Pro Microphone*.\n- For any app, including standalone Ghostty and TextEdit. Text appears live; stop with Globe twice, Esc, or a click on the mic.\n\n**Shortcut hygiene**\n- Don't give any system-wide STT (macOS Dictation, Whispering) **Cmd+E**, or it will take the key from Orca.\n- Avoid **Cmd+D** as a global shortcut: it's Ghostty's default split-right, and Orca may use it too.\n\n## 5. DJI wireless mic: preventing sleep\n\n- **Transmitter Auto Off** shuts the transmitter down after about 15 min with no receiver link and no internal recording. Afterwards it needs a manual power press.\n  - **Mic 2 / Mic 3** (receiver has a touchscreen): swipe down → **Transmitter Settings → Transmitter Auto Off → OFF**. Also turn off the receiver's own auto power-off.\n  - **Mic Mini** (receiver has no screen): change the same settings in the **DJI Mimo** app.\n- **Power-saving sleep** can't be disabled. If the transmitter loses the receiver signal (e.g. the Mac sleeps), it dozes and reconnects on its own when the signal returns, so the first second or so of dictation may be lost.\n- Tradeoff: with auto-off disabled, a forgotten transmitter will drain its battery. Power it off or dock it when you're done.\n\nSources:\n[DJI Mic Series Intelligent Features Overview](https://support.dji.com/help/content?customId=01700009936&spaceId=17&re=US&lang=en&paperDocType=ARTICLE) ·\n[DJI Mic Mini 2 / Mic 2 Auto Power Off](https://support.dji.com/help/content?customId=en-us03400009936&spaceId=34&re=US&lang=en&documentType=artical&paperDocType=paper) ·\n[DJI Forum: Disabling Mic 2 Auto Power Off](https://forum.dji.com/thread-306449-1-1.html) ·\n[heliguy: Mic Mini power-saving](https://www.heliguy.com/blogs/knowledge-base/does-dji-mic-mini-support-automatic-power-saving-and-auto-shutdown-after-inactivity/)\n\n## 6. Quick-check runbook (next time STT breaks)\n\nRun in **Terminal.app on the MacBook** (not an Orca pane; those run on the Studio):\n```sh\nhostname                                   # must be Jons-MacBook-Pro*, not Mac-Studio\npython3 -c \"import json;d=json.load(open('$HOME/Library/Application Support/orca/profiles/local-default/orca-data.json'));print(d['settings']['voice'])\"\ncat ~/.orca/keybindings.json 2>/dev/null   # any override of voice.dictation?\nls \"$HOME/Library/Application Support/orca/speech-models/\"\nps -axo comm | grep -iE 'karabiner|raycast|hammerspoon|skhd|bettertouch|whisper|wispr' | sort -u\np=$(ioreg -l -w 0 | grep -o '\"kCGSSessionSecureInputPID\"=[0-9]*' | head -1 | cut -d= -f2); [ -n \"$p\" ] && ps -o comm= -p \"$p\"\n```\nChecklist:\n1. `sttModel` is non-empty and the model directory exists → otherwise Orca → Settings → Voice → download the model.\n2. Orca has microphone permission (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone).\n3. No other app has a global Cmd+E; Secure Input isn't held by an app you're actively using (fix with lock/unlock, Ctrl+Cmd+Q).\n4. For Dictation, or Orca with the default mic: the DJI transmitter is on and the input meter moves (System Settings → Sound → Input).\n5. After an Orca update, re-check that `settings.voice` survived (the MacBook is on 1.4.215, the Studio on 1.4.210).\n\n## 7. Open items / housekeeping\n\n- The Studio's `~/.ssh/known_hosts` now includes the MacBook's host key (from the failed SSH probe). Harmless; remove with `ssh-keygen -R 100.82.72.91` if unwanted.\n- No keys were installed and no settings were changed by the agent on either machine; every fix was applied by the user in the GUI.\n- Optional: give the Studio key-based SSH to the MacBook (append the Studio's `~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub`, fingerprint `SHA256:kz0Ub8…AjkA`, to the MacBook's `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`) so future MacBook diagnostics can run remotely.\n- Optional: align Orca versions (Studio 1.4.210 vs MacBook 1.4.215).\n- The Studio's Orca also has a stale 1.4.207 crashpad handler and an older pty-daemon lineage running; a clean Orca restart on the Studio would tidy that.\n- Whispering (`com.bradenwong.whispering`) is installed on the Studio but not running. Cmd+E now works |\n| Cmd+E did nothing in standalone Ghostty | Expected: Orca's dictation is scoped to Orca windows, and Ghostty has no STT and no Cmd+E binding | Use a system-wide STT (macOS Dictation or Whispering) for non-Orca apps |\n| macOS Dictation showed the blue mic in TextEdit but produced no text | Mic source \"Automatic\" picked **Wireless Mic Rx** (DJI receiver) while the DJI transmitter was asleep or off, so it was sending silence | Woke the transmitter; Dictation now transcribes |\n| DJI transmitter keeps going to sleep | DJI **Transmitter Auto Off** (about 15 min with no link) plus non-disableable power-saving sleep | Receiver → swipe down → Transmitter Settings → Transmitter Auto Off = OFF (Mic Mini: DJI Mimo app) |\n\nFinal state: **Orca Cmd+E dictation works (Parakeet v3); macOS Dictation works (Globe twice); DJI mic works when awake.**\n\n## 1. Environment (the key discovery)\n\nThe problem report said \"this MacBook\", but the Claude session was running on a **different machine**.\nOrca runs as a host runtime on the Mac Studio with the MacBook attached as a remote client, so\nOrca terminal panes on the MacBook execute their shells on the Mac Studio.\n\n| | Mac Studio (runtime host) | MacBook Pro (where you type) |\n|---|---|---|\n| Hostname / model | `Mac-Studio` / `Mac16,9` | `Jons-MacBook-Pro-7.local` / `Mac16,1` |\n| Tailscale IP | 100.126.217.74 | 100.82.72.91 (`jons-macbook-pro`) |\n| Orca version | 1.4.210 | 1.4.215 |\n| Orca voice `sttModel` (before fix) | `parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-int8` (downloaded 2026-09-23) | `\"\"` (none) |\n| Physical keyboard | none connected (Magic Keyboard \"Not Connected\") | built-in, plus an external PC-layout keyboard (vendor 9610 / product 73) |\n| Secure Input | held by `loginwindow` (PID 1340): screen locked, normal for a headless host | none |\n\nHow the topology was established:\n- `echo $TERM_PROGRAM` → `Orca`; the parent chain of the session is an `Orca Helper` on the Studio.\n- `~/Library/Application Support/orca/orca-devices.json` on the Studio lists a paired **\"Runtime 9/24/2026\"** device, `lastSeenAt` within about 45 s of \"now\".\n- `lsof -nP -iTCP:6768 -sTCP:ESTABLISHED` → Orca (pid 740) has websocket connections from **100.82.72.91**.\n- `tailscale status` → 100.82.72.91 = `jons-macbook-pro`.\n\n**Lesson:** anything typed into an Orca pane runs on the **Studio**. The first MacBook diagnostic run\ncame back with Studio data (same `loginwindow` PID 1340, same voice settings). Diagnostics for\nthe MacBook must run in **Terminal.app on the MacBook** (check `hostname` first).\n\n## 2. How Orca dictation works (from the 1.4.210 app bundle)\n\nExtracted `/Applications/Orca.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar` (via `npx @electron/asar extract`) and traced the key path:\n\n1. **Keybinding table** (`keybindings-*.js`): `{id: \"voice.dictation\", title: \"Dictation\", scope: \"global\", defaultBindings: [\"Mod+E\"]}`. `Mod+E` is the *only* default use of Cmd+E in Orca.\n2. **Main process** (`main/index.js`), `webContents.on(\"before-input-event\")`: the key maps to `{type: \"dictationKeyDown\"}`, then:\n   ```js\n   let t = settings.voice;\n   return !t?.enabled || !t.sttModel || (t.dictationMode ?? \"toggle\") === \"hold\"\n     ? false                                         // NOT handled → key falls through to the pane\n     : (e.preventDefault(), webContents.send(\"ui:dictationKeyDown\"), true)\n   ```\n3. **Renderer** (`DictationController-*.js`): `onDictationKeyDown` starts or stops recording only if `voice.enabled && voice.sttModel`.\n4. **Engine**: `Resources/node_modules/sherpa-onnx-darwin-arm64/` (sherpa-onnx + onnxruntime 1.23.2) runs in `stt-worker.js`. Models are downloaded from Hugging Face (`csukuangfj/sherpa-onnx-nemo-parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-int8`) into `~/Library/Application Support/orca/speech-models/<model>/` (`encoder.int8.onnx` is about 652 MB, plus decoder, joiner and `tokens.txt`).\n\nSo with `sttModel: \"\"`, Orca deliberately returns `false`, Cmd+E is passed to the terminal, and nothing starts. This explains the MacBook symptom exactly.\n\nRelevant settings, in `~/Library/Application Support/orca/profiles/local-default/orca-data.json` → `settings.voice`:\n```json\n{\"enabled\": true, \"sttModel\": \"parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-int8\", \"modelsDir\": \"\", \"language\": \"en\",\n \"dictationMode\": \"toggle\", \"terminalConfirmBeforeInsert\": false, \"microphoneDeviceId\": null}\n```\nCustom keybindings would live in `~/.orca/keybindings.json` (absent on both machines, so defaults apply).\n`settings.terminalShortcutPolicy = \"orca-first\"`.\n\n## 3. Debugging timeline\n\n1. **Explored the Studio (wrong machine, useful baseline).** Found Orca (Electron 43.7, v1.4.210), Ghostty, and Whispering (installed, not running).\n   All Studio-side checks passed:\n   - The keybinding is the default `Mod+E`, with no user override.\n   - The only plugin, `stablyai.orca-navigation-shortcuts`, binds `Mod+Alt+T/F/G`, so it doesn't conflict.\n   - No hotkey or remap apps are running (Karabiner, Raycast, BTT, Hammerspoon, skhd, …); `hidutil` UserKeyMapping is `(null)`; there are no `NSUserKeyEquivalents`.\n   - Mic TCC: `com.stablyai.orca` allowed (2026-09-23), and the app has the `com.apple.security.device.audio-input` entitlement.\n   - Speech engine and model files are present.\n2. **Tried to send Cmd+E via `osascript`/System Events.** It hung on an Automation permission prompt, so I killed it.\n   If a \"Orca wants to control System Events\" dialog appeared, answer *Don't Allow*.\n3. **User symptom report:** Cmd+E, with or without Shift, does nothing on the first press and types `e` on repeat presses, in both Orca and Ghostty.\n   That pointed below the app layer. The Orca lock file named the host `Mac-Studio.local`, which led to the topology discovery in §1.\n4. **SSH to the MacBook** (`ssh -o BatchMode=yes jonc@100.82.72.91`): Remote Login is on but password-only, so no key access.\n   Stopped rather than work around it. Side effect: the MacBook's ED25519 host key was added to the Studio's `~/.ssh/known_hosts`.\n5. **First \"MacBook\" diagnostics were really Studio output** (run from an Orca pane): the same `loginwindow` Secure Input PID 1340, identical voice settings. Re-ran in Terminal.app.\n6. **Real MacBook diagnostics:**\n   - The TextEdit test (Cmd+C/V, Cmd+T) worked normally, so the Command key is fine.\n   - No Secure Input and no hotkey apps; UniversalControl only.\n   - `hidutil` is `(null)`.\n   - `modifiermapping.0-0-0` (built-in keyboard) is identity.\n   - `modifiermapping.9610-73-0` (external PC keyboard) swaps Cmd↔Option on both sides. That's the usual setup for a PC-layout keyboard and not the cause (usage `0xE2`=L-Opt, `0xE3`=L-Cmd, `0xE6`=R-Opt, `0xE7`=R-Cmd).\n   - **Orca voice `sttModel: ''`**: this was the root cause.\n7. **Fix applied by the user:** selected and downloaded Parakeet v3 in MacBook Orca → **Cmd+E works**.\n8. **macOS Dictation (for non-Orca apps).** Enabled with a Cmd+D shortcut. The blue mic showed in TextEdit but produced no text.\n   - Clarified that Dictation streams text live; there is no separate stop-and-transcribe step. Stop it with the shortcut, Esc, or by clicking the mic.\n   - Changed the shortcut to **Press Globe twice**, because Cmd+D is Ghostty's default \"split right\" and a system-wide shortcut would take it away from every app.\n   - Mic source \"Automatic\" had picked **Wireless Mic Rx** (the DJI receiver). The transmitter was asleep, so it was sending silence. Turning the transmitter on fixed it.\n9. **DJI transmitter sleep:** see §5.\n\n## 4. Final configuration\n\n**MacBook, Orca (Settings → Voice)**\n- Voice: enabled · Model: `parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-int8` (local, offline) · Mode: toggle · Language: en\n- Shortcut: **Cmd+E** (default `voice.dictation`); press once to start and again to stop. Works only while an Orca window has focus.\n\n**MacBook, macOS Dictation (System Settings → Keyboard → Dictation)**\n- On · Shortcut: **Press Globe (🌐) twice** · Language: English (US), on-device model downloaded\n- Microphone source: Automatic, which currently resolves to **Wireless Mic Rx** (DJI). If Dictation shows the mic but types nothing, check the transmitter first, or pin the source to *MacBook Pro Microphone*.\n- For any app, including standalone Ghostty and TextEdit. Text appears live; stop with Globe twice, Esc, or a click on the mic.\n\n**Shortcut hygiene**\n- Don't give any system-wide STT (macOS Dictation, Whispering) **Cmd+E**, or it will take the key from Orca.\n- Avoid **Cmd+D** as a global shortcut: it's Ghostty's default split-right, and Orca may use it too.\n\n## 5. DJI wireless mic: preventing sleep\n\n- **Transmitter Auto Off** shuts the transmitter down after about 15 min with no receiver link and no internal recording. Afterwards it needs a manual power press.\n  - **Mic 2 / Mic 3** (receiver has a touchscreen): swipe down → **Transmitter Settings → Transmitter Auto Off → OFF**. Also turn off the receiver's own auto power-off.\n  - **Mic Mini** (receiver has no screen): change the same settings in the **DJI Mimo** app.\n- **Power-saving sleep** can't be disabled. If the transmitter loses the receiver signal (e.g. the Mac sleeps), it dozes and reconnects on its own when the signal returns, so the first second or so of dictation may be lost.\n- Tradeoff: with auto-off disabled, a forgotten transmitter will drain its battery. Power it off or dock it when you're done.\n\nSources:\n[DJI Mic Series Intelligent Features Overview](https://support.dji.com/help/content?customId=01700009936&spaceId=17&re=US&lang=en&paperDocType=ARTICLE) ·\n[DJI Mic Mini 2 / Mic 2 Auto Power Off](https://support.dji.com/help/content?customId=en-us03400009936&spaceId=34&re=US&lang=en&documentType=artical&paperDocType=paper) ·\n[DJI Forum: Disabling Mic 2 Auto Power Off](https://forum.dji.com/thread-306449-1-1.html) ·\n[heliguy: Mic Mini power-saving](https://www.heliguy.com/blogs/knowledge-base/does-dji-mic-mini-support-automatic-power-saving-and-auto-shutdown-after-inactivity/)\n\n## 6. Quick-check runbook (next time STT breaks)\n\nRun in **Terminal.app on the MacBook** (not an Orca pane; those run on the Studio):\n```sh\nhostname                                   # must be Jons-MacBook-Pro*, not Mac-Studio\npython3 -c \"import json;d=json.load(open('$HOME/Library/Application Support/orca/profiles/local-default/orca-data.json'));print(d['settings']['voice'])\"\ncat ~/.orca/keybindings.json 2>/dev/null   # any override of voice.dictation?\nls \"$HOME/Library/Application Support/orca/speech-models/\"\nps -axo comm | grep -iE 'karabiner|raycast|hammerspoon|skhd|bettertouch|whisper|wispr' | sort -u\np=$(ioreg -l -w 0 | grep -o '\"kCGSSessionSecureInputPID\"=[0-9]*' | head -1 | cut -d= -f2); [ -n \"$p\" ] && ps -o comm= -p \"$p\"\n```\nChecklist:\n1. `sttModel` is non-empty and the model directory exists → otherwise Orca → Settings → Voice → download the model.\n2. Orca has microphone permission (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone).\n3. No other app has a global Cmd+E; Secure Input isn't held by an app you're actively using (fix with lock/unlock, Ctrl+Cmd+Q).\n4. For Dictation, or Orca with the default mic: the DJI transmitter is on and the input meter moves (System Settings → Sound → Input).\n5. After an Orca update, re-check that `settings.voice` survived (the MacBook is on 1.4.215, the Studio on 1.4.210).\n\n## 7. Open items / housekeeping\n\n- The Studio's `~/.ssh/known_hosts` now includes the MacBook's host key (from the failed SSH probe). Harmless; remove with `ssh-keygen -R 100.82.72.91` if unwanted.\n- No keys were installed and no settings were changed by the agent on either machine; every fix was applied by the user in the GUI.\n- Optional: give the Studio key-based SSH to the MacBook (append the Studio's `~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub`, fingerprint `SHA256:kz0Ub8…AjkA`, to the MacBook's `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`) so future MacBook diagnostics can run remotely.\n- Optional: align Orca versions (Studio 1.4.210 vs MacBook 1.4.215).\n- The Studio's Orca also has a stale 1.4.207 crashpad handler and an older pty-daemon lineage running; a clean Orca restart on the Studio would tidy that.\n- Whispering (`com.bradenwong.whispering`) is installed on the Studio but not running. It isn't needed now that macOS Dictation works.\n"}},"apiBlockIndex":0,"requestId":"req_011CfYC9VdRsnPH17o6Z26CN","type":"assistant","uuid":"c44788a9-739d-4a09-9c38-e59820679b18","timestamp":"2026-09-29T18:21:02.338Z","advisorModel":"claude-fable-5-1","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"c73d83ab-25a7-4591-bc61-455c6b5a4045","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/jonc/code/iphs400-mp2-cms-starter","sessionId":"c73d83ab-25a7-4591-bc61-455c6b5a4045","version":"2.1.284","gitBranch":"main"}

How Orca dictation works (from the 1.4.210 app bundle)\n\nExtracted `/Applications/Orca.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar` (via `npx @electron/asar extract`) and traced the key path:\n\n1. **Keybinding table** (`keybindings-*.js`): `{id: \"voice.dictation\", title: \"Dictation\", scope: \"global\", defaultBindings: [\"Mod+E\"]}`. `Mod+E` is the *only* default use of Cmd+E in Orca.\n2. **Main process** (`main/index.js`), `webContents.on(\"before-input-event\")`: the key maps to `{type: \"dictationKeyDown\"}`, then:\n   ```js\n   let t = settings.voice;\n   return !t?.enabled || !t.sttModel || (t.dictationMode ?? \"toggle\") === \"hold\"\n     ? false                                         // NOT handled → key falls through to the pane\n     : (e.preventDefault(), webContents.send(\"ui:dictationKeyDown\"), true)\n   ```\n3. **Renderer** (`DictationController-*.js`): `onDictationKeyDown` starts or stops recording only if `voice.enabled && voice.sttModel`.\n4. **Engine**: `Resources/node_modules/sherpa-onnx-darwin-arm64/` (sherpa-onnx + onnxruntime 1.23.2) runs in `stt-worker.js`. Models are downloaded from Hugging Face (`csukuangfj/sherpa-onnx-nemo-parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-int8`) into `~/Library/Application Support/orca/speech-models/<model>/` (`encoder.int8.onnx` is about 652 MB, plus decoder, joiner and `tokens.txt`).\n\nSo with `sttModel: \"\"`, Orca deliberately returns `false`, Cmd+E is passed to the terminal, and nothing starts. This explains the MacBook symptom exactly.\n\nRelevant settings, in `~/Library/Application Support/orca/profiles/local-default/orca-data.json` → `settings.voice`:\n```json\n{\"enabled\": true, \"sttModel\": \"parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-int8\", \"modelsDir\": \"\", \"language\": \"en\",\n \"dictationMode\": \"toggle\", \"terminalConfirmBeforeInsert\": false, \"microphoneDeviceId\": null}\n```\nCustom keybindings would live in `~/.orca/keybindings.json` (absent on both machines, so defaults apply).\n`settings.terminalShortcutPolicy = \"orca-first\"`.\n\n## 3. Debugging timeline\n\n1. **Explored the Studio (wrong machine, useful baseline).** Found Orca (Electron 43.7, v1.4.210), Ghostty, and Whispering (installed, not running).\n   All Studio-side checks passed:\n   - The keybinding is the default `Mod+E`, with no user override.\n   - The only plugin, `stablyai.orca-navigation-shortcuts`, binds `Mod+Alt+T/F/G`, so it doesn't conflict.\n   - No hotkey or remap apps are running (Karabiner, Raycast, BTT, Hammerspoon, skhd, …); `hidutil` UserKeyMapping is `(null)`; there are no `NSUserKeyEquivalents`.\n   - Mic TCC: `com.stablyai.orca` allowed (2026-09-23), and the app has the `com.apple.security.device.audio-input` entitlement.\n   - Speech engine and model files are present.\n2. **Tried to send Cmd+E via `osascript`/System Events.** It hung on an Automation permission prompt, so I killed it.\n   If a \"Orca wants to control System Events\" dialog appeared, answer *Don't Allow*.\n3. **User symptom report:** Cmd+E, with or without Shift, does nothing on the first press and types `e` on repeat presses, in both Orca and Ghostty.\n   That pointed below the app layer. The Orca lock file named the host `Mac-Studio.local`, which led to the topology discovery in §1.\n4. **SSH to the MacBook** (`ssh -o BatchMode=yes jonc@100.82.72.91`): Remote Login is on but password-only, so no key access.\n   Stopped rather than work around it. Side effect: the MacBook's ED25519 host key was added to the Studio's `~/.ssh/known_hosts`.\n5. **First \"MacBook\" diagnostics were really Studio output** (run from an Orca pane): the same `loginwindow` Secure Input PID 1340, identical voice settings. Re-ran in Terminal.app.\n6. **Real MacBook diagnostics:**\n   - The TextEdit test (Cmd+C/V, Cmd+T) worked normally, so the Command key is fine.\n   - No Secure Input and no hotkey apps; UniversalControl only.\n   - `hidutil` is `(null)`.\n   - `modifiermapping.0-0-0` (built-in keyboard) is identity.\n   - `modifiermapping.9610-73-0` (external PC keyboard) swaps Cmd↔Option on both sides. That's the usual setup for a PC-layout keyboard and not the cause (usage `0xE2`=L-Opt, `0xE3`=L-Cmd, `0xE6`=R-Opt, `0xE7`=R-Cmd).\n   - **Orca voice `sttModel: ''`**: this was the root cause.\n7. **Fix applied by the user:** selected and downloaded Parakeet v3 in MacBook Orca → **Cmd+E works**.\n8. **macOS Dictation (for non-Orca apps).** Enabled with a Cmd+D shortcut. The blue mic showed in TextEdit but produced no text.\n   - Clarified that Dictation streams text live; there is no separate stop-and-transcribe step. Stop it with the shortcut, Esc, or by clicking the mic.\n   - Changed the shortcut to **Press Globe twice**, because Cmd+D is Ghostty's default \"split right\" and a system-wide shortcut would take it away from every app.\n   - Mic source \"Automatic\" had picked **Wireless Mic Rx** (the DJI receiver). The transmitter was asleep, so it was sending silence. Turning the transmitter on fixed it.\n9. **DJI transmitter sleep:** see §5.\n\n## 4. Final configuration\n\n**MacBook, Orca (Settings → Voice)**\n- Voice: enabled · Model: `parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-int8` (local, offline) · Mode: toggle · Language: en\n- Shortcut: **Cmd+E** (default `voice.dictation`); press once to start and again to stop. Works only while an Orca window has focus.\n\n**MacBook, macOS Dictation (System Settings → Keyboard → Dictation)**\n- On · Shortcut: **Press Globe (🌐) twice** · Language: English (US), on-device model downloaded\n- Microphone source: Automatic, which currently resolves to **Wireless Mic Rx** (DJI). If Dictation shows the mic but types nothing, check the transmitter first, or pin the source to *MacBook Pro Microphone*.\n- For any app, including standalone Ghostty and TextEdit. Text appears live; stop with Globe twice, Esc, or a click on the mic.\n\n**Shortcut hygiene**\n- Don't give any system-wide STT (macOS Dictation, Whispering) **Cmd+E**, or it will take the key from Orca.\n- Avoid **Cmd+D** as a global shortcut: it's Ghostty's default split-right, and Orca may use it too.\n\n## 5. DJI wireless mic: preventing sleep\n\n- **Transmitter Auto Off** shuts the transmitter down after about 15 min with no receiver link and no internal recording. Afterwards it needs a manual power press.\n  - **Mic 2 / Mic 3** (receiver has a touchscreen): swipe down → **Transmitter Settings → Transmitter Auto Off → OFF**. Also turn off the receiver's own auto power-off.\n  - **Mic Mini** (receiver has no screen): change the same settings in the **DJI Mimo** app.\n- **Power-saving sleep** can't be disabled. If the transmitter loses the receiver signal (e.g. the Mac sleeps), it dozes and reconnects on its own when the signal returns, so the first second or so of dictation may be lost.\n- Tradeoff: with auto-off disabled, a forgotten transmitter will drain its battery. Power it off or dock it when you're done.\n\nSources:\n[DJI Mic Series Intelligent Features Overview](https://support.dji.com/help/content?customId=01700009936&spaceId=17&re=US&lang=en&paperDocType=ARTICLE) ·\n[DJI Mic Mini 2 / Mic 2 Auto Power Off](https://support.dji.com/help/content?customId=en-us03400009936&spaceId=34&re=US&lang=en&documentType=artical&paperDocType=paper) ·\n[DJI Forum: Disabling Mic 2 Auto Power Off](https://forum.dji.com/thread-306449-1-1.html) ·\n[heliguy: Mic Mini power-saving](https://www.heliguy.com/blogs/knowledge-base/does-dji-mic-mini-support-automatic-power-saving-and-auto-shutdown-after-inactivity/)\n\n## 6. Quick-check runbook (next time STT breaks)\n\nRun in **Terminal.app on the MacBook** (not an Orca pane; those run on the Studio):\n```sh\nhostname                                   # must be Jons-MacBook-Pro*, not Mac-Studio\npython3 -c \"import json;d=json.load(open('$HOME/Library/Application Support/orca/profiles/local-default/orca-data.json'));print(d['settings']['voice'])\"\ncat ~/.orca/keybindings.json 2>/dev/null   # any override of voice.dictation?\nls \"$HOME/Library/Application Support/orca/speech-models/\"\nps -axo comm | grep -iE 'karabiner|raycast|hammerspoon|skhd|bettertouch|whisper|wispr' | sort -u\np=$(ioreg -l -w 0 | grep -o '\"kCGSSessionSecureInputPID\"=[0-9]*' | head -1 | cut -d= -f2); [ -n \"$p\" ] && ps -o comm= -p \"$p\"\n```\nChecklist:\n1. `sttModel` is non-empty and the model directory exists → otherwise Orca → Settings → Voice → download the model.\n2. Orca has microphone permission (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone).\n3. No other app has a global Cmd+E; Secure Input isn't held by an app you're actively using (fix with lock/unlock, Ctrl+Cmd+Q).\n4. For Dictation, or Orca with the default mic: the DJI transmitter is on and the input meter moves (System Settings → Sound → Input).\n5. After an Orca update, re-check that `settings.voice` survived (the MacBook is on 1.4.215, the Studio on 1.4.210).\n\n## 7. Open items / housekeeping\n\n- The Studio's `~/.ssh/known_hosts` now includes the MacBook's host key (from the failed SSH probe). Harmless; remove with `ssh-keygen -R 100.82.72.91` if unwanted.\n- No keys were installed and no settings were changed by the agent on either machine; every fix was applied by the user in the GUI.\n- Optional: give the Studio key-based SSH to the MacBook (append the Studio's `~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub`, fingerprint `SHA256:kz0Ub8…AjkA`, to the MacBook's `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`) so future MacBook diagnostics can run remotely.\n- Optional: align Orca versions (Studio 1.4.210 vs MacBook 1.4.215).\n- The Studio's Orca also has a stale 1.4.207 crashpad handler and an older pty-daemon lineage running; a clean Orca restart on the Studio would tidy that.\n- Whispering (`com.bradenwong.whispering`) is installed on the Studio but not running. Dictation typed nothing because it picked the DJI receiver while the transmitter was asleep. And the DJI transmitter shuts itself off automatically.\n- **§1 Setup:** Orca runs on the Mac Studio and the MacBook connects to it as a client, so an Orca pane on the MacBook runs its shell on the Studio.
